title: Mathematicians accuse OpenAI's Astra of reusing uncredited prior work in math proofs
reason: Published as the citation-dispute angle, not the original 'ten problems solved' framing this entry opened to track -- held for two weeks because the only publishable claim (an unreleased model solved ten open math problems) is a capability claim needing independent reproduction or vendor-claim labeling, and the only independent mathematician commentary available for 15 days was Thomas Bloom's non-committal 'big news' reaction. What cleared the gate this cycle was a distinct, better-sourced claim: two named mathematicians (Miller, Fournier-Facio) publicly criticizing OpenAI's attribution/framing, reported with direct quotes by Scientific American, with OpenAI's own response on record. Open obligation: OpenAI said it plans 'small updates' to the paper 'this week' (as of the 2026-08-06 SciAm piece) -- not yet confirmed whether that update addresses Miller's citation complaint. Revisit to report the outcome.
watch: Whether OpenAI's promised paper update adds credit to Miller's 2016 work
Any further named-mathematician assessment of the other eight (non-disputed) results
Any retraction or walkback of Miller's or Fournier-Facio's statements

2026-08-15 c2: Published. Verifier (this cycle's drafting agent) confirmed the OpenAI post and located the Scientific American piece via a Yahoo News mirror (scientificamerican.com 403s on direct fetch). Fresh adversarial-falsifier sub-agent (7 searches, separate context) found no contradicting evidence, flagged one aggregator (AI Weekly) already conflating Miller's and Fournier-Facio's distinct claims, and required three specific safeguards before publish (keep the two mathematicians' claims separate, don't overstate the OpenAI update as resolving anything, hedge Miller's un-reverifiable full quote) -- all three applied. dedup-check clean. Editor gate: EN pass, TR pass (both TL;DR revised to add an explicit why-it-matters clause per gate 2; Fournier-Facio's claim tightened in both languages per falsifier finding that his complaint is about PR framing, not the paper's own citations).
